_howto: Newest first. Add an entry at the top each time you push an update; the website and the in-game 'What's new' both read this file. tag: new | improved | fixed.

items.text: Stats and Records now live inside the Legacy tab (Legacy · Stats · Records), so the top bar has 7 tabs instead of 9.

People is grouped: Inner circle, On the course (whoever has challenged Ryan, with the head-to-head and the last run-in), Casino staff (dealers and servers you've met, with their tier, visits and tips), and Casino regulars (the craps regulars at tables you've rolled at).
Each casino's craps regulars now count Ryan's rolls at their table. The familiarity labels (New face, Nodding terms, Table regular, Rail family) are drafts. Counting starts with this update.
Men on the PGA ladder no longer carry the surname form “Petrova”.

notes.title: The road to the PGA Tour

items.text: Until phase 3, Ryan is chasing a PGA Tour card: PGA Tour Q-School (First, Second and Final Stage), then the Korn Ferry Tour, then the PGA Tour. Coach Dana, the inbox, the schedule, trophies and achievements all say so.
Every field Ryan plays before phase 3 is a men's field, all the way up the ladder. Older saves are brought over on load: same golfers, ids and ratings.
Kayla stays on the women's tours (LPGA Q-School, Epson Tour, LPGA Tour), so you'll follow her in the news and on the People screen rather than on your leaderboards for now.
Amateur and major names lost their “Women's”: the Inland Empire Amateur, SoCal Amateur, State Amateur Championship, Championship of the Americas, National Open Championship and Alpine Championship.
If the bank drops under $100, an “Ask Baba for help” card appears on the Career screen. Baba sends $500, one time per career. The weekly rent warning mentions it while it's unused.
Paying Baba back is optional: no interest, no deadline. Once the bank reaches $1,000 the card offers it, and Baba notices (he pretends not to).
Ryan is “he” in Act I: fixed the albatross headline and a couple of notes that said “her”.

notes.title: Faces at the craps rail, and no more spoilers

items.text: The craps regulars have portraits now: all nine, each grinning after a win and groaning after a loss. Ryan's seat shows his too.

Spin to Win no longer gives the result away before the wheel stops: the spin history, the win and every bank figure now wait until it lands, with a short pause before the result. Keno, video poker and craps hold the bank the same way until the last ball, card or die is shown.

notes.title: The regulars are official, and a new welcome

items.text: The nine craps regulars and everything they say are now final, along with Stick Lady's hot and cold calls. Portraits are on the way.
A new career starts with a better welcome letter that previews the road ahead, with a word about Baba.

notes.title: Craps comes alive, and you bet on the felt

items.text: Bet right on the craps table, like at baccarat: tap the Pass Line, the Field, Come, a number, a hardway or a one-roll bet on the felt itself. Once a point is on, tapping your Pass or Don't Pass bet again puts odds behind it. The full bet list is still one tap away (and open by default on phones).
Craps has regulars now: three characters at each casino's table, each with their own way of betting and plenty to say. They bet pretend money on the same dice as you.

The dice pass around the table after every seven-out, and when it's Ryan's turn you shoot. A meter shows when the table runs hot, on fire or cold, built from what the dice actually did. The dice themselves are always fair.
The table's rail, your chips and the Roll button sit right under the craps table.

Hardways (hard 6 and 8 pay 9 to 1, hard 4 and 10 pay 7 to 1) and the one-roll bets: Any Seven, Any Craps, 2, 3, 11, 12 and the Horn. The centre of every craps table now shows the right payouts and your bets.

The craps betting area is laid out like the table itself: the Don't Come bar and the numbers across the top, then Come, the Field, Don't Pass and the Pass Line, with the hardways and one-roll bets in the centre.

notes.title: Full craps (part 1) and Spin to Win

items.text: Craps now has Come and Don't Come bets, Place bets on 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 10, and lay odds behind Don't Pass and Don't Come. Your bets ride from roll to roll and stay on the table if you leave or reload. Place bets and odds can be taken down. Hardways and one-roll bets come next.

Spin to Win: the classic money wheel, with a machine of its own at every casino. Bet on $1, $2, $5, $10, $20, the casino's emblem or the star, then spin. The wheel has 54 equal slots, so what you see is the real odds: up to 40 to 1.

notes.title: New card tables, and two more casinos open

items.text: New tables for Blackjack, Three Card Poker and Baccarat at every casino, each with its own printed felt, chip rack, deck and shoe. Chips land on the printed spots. The dealer still stands on all 17s.

The White Buffalo and Morongo Sky are open. Reach $100,000 or $1,000,000 in the bank to unlock them, then pick one in the lobby: every game is there, on that casino's own tables, machines and chips, with its own drink server. The Desert Palms dealers and Emmett cover the shifts until those casinos hire their own.
A night out still uses one activity; once you're in, walking over to another unlocked casino that night is free. The White Buffalo and Morongo Sky sportsbooks take bigger bets ($2,500 and $10,000).
A new Video Poker & Keno machine on the casino floor: one cabinet, two games, switch between them on top. No dealer, but the drink server still comes round.
Video poker is Jacks or Better on the full-pay 9/6 table: hold cards (tap them or press 1–5), draw, and bet max for the 4,000-coin Royal Flush. A dealt hand is still waiting for you after a reload.
Keno: pick 1 to 10 of 80 numbers, twenty balls are drawn and the pay card pays on how many you catch. Quick pick, and your ticket stays picked for the next game.
Each casino's machine has its own look: Desert Palms keno with palms and a sunset, plus White Buffalo and Morongo Sky versions ready for when those casinos open. In-game money only.

notes.title: Sports history moves into the sportsbook

items.text: The Sports History Board now lives in the sportsbook instead of the main menu: press History at the sportsbook to open the full archive on the league you were watching, and ◀ Sportsbook (or Esc) to get back to the lines.

Behind the scenes: the four leagues' complete history (every season, game, champion, award and record) is now packaged for Tiny Mana's NPC Factory, so future characters can talk sports history accurately and at their own level of fandom.
Every one of the 25,800 games in the four leagues' history was re-checked: schedules, records, playoffs, box scores and records all add up.
Emmett's stories at the Palms Sports Bar are easier to read.

A new Sports History tab: fifty-plus years of the four leagues in one almanac. Browse every season's standings and playoffs, every champion, award and record, the Hall of Fame and the league's great moments.
Look up any player, from the 1970s founders to this year's rookies, with season-by-season stats, awards and titles. Your career's own seasons appear alongside the history as they're played.
A newspaper-style Year in Review for every completed season.

From 2028 the four leagues keep evolving with your career: players age, improve and decline, retire, and are replaced through a yearly draft. Champions, awards, records and Hall of Fame classes build up season after season, and every career's sports history goes its own way.
When a new season starts, your Inbox gets the sports year in review: champions, retirements, rookies and Hall of Fame inductees.
Every bet settles against the exact game it was priced on, and a season you've already bet on or watched never changes.

notes.title: The leagues' own players take the field

items.text: The sportsbook's 32 teams now field the real players from fifty years of league history, carried through a simulated 2026 season, retirements and two drafts. New careers start with them.
Existing careers switch at the start of next season if you have bets on this one, so every open ticket settles on exactly the game you bet on. Your bankroll and ticket history are unchanged.

notes.title: Fifty years of awards and records

items.text: Behind the scenes, every league now has its full honours history: MVPs, rookies of the year, championship MVPs, stat leaders, record books, draft classes and a proposed Hall of Fame, all worked out from the simulated games. They'll show up at the sportsbook in a later update.

The four leagues have new names: the Grand Diamond League (baseball), the Crown Ball League (basketball), Amigo League Football and the Federal Hockey League. Your bets, tickets and history carry over unchanged.
Hockey playoff games tied after regulation now play full sudden-death overtime periods, with no shootouts, just like real playoff hockey.

Emmett at the Desert Palms sportsbook now talks sports history: legends, famous finals and old grudges for whichever sport you're looking at, plus quick notes on this season. Tap him or press "Another one" for the next story.
Sports history: Elias Voss's legendary 1983 is now 13–1 with three no-hitters, and Miami is the 2009 basketball champion.
Emmett's greeting at the sportsbook counter no longer carries a Placeholder tag.
Sportsbook bets now use your real bankroll. Lines, scores and standings come from the live leagues, and every game shows its week and day.
When you advance the week, finished bets settle and pay out automatically, and a note in your Inbox tells you what won and lost, with the final scores.
The Tickets screen shows your open bets, a full history of settled tickets and your running record and net.
Baseball games are more evenly matched, so lines look like real baseball.

notes.title: A history board you can read

items.text: On iPhone and iPad, scenes like Biff's driving range could lose their pictures after a long session. The golf course and clubhouse now hand their graphics memory back when you leave them.

The sportsbook History board is now split into About, Champions, Moments, Legends and Teams, so nothing hides below the screen. Tap a team to see its titles, big moments, rivals and how its fans talk.
Sports history updates: the basketball league had eight founding clubs, and Las Vegas beat two higher seeds on its 1996 title run.
On phones, the driving range no longer repeats at the top of the picture during Biff's long-drive challenge.

The sportsbook History board now tells each league's story: when it was founded, its trophy, the champions on record and its most famous moments, from the 71-Save Night to the Phantom Touchdown. This history is still a draft.
Seasons the history hasn't covered yet are shown as unwritten instead of with made-up champions.
Emmett Okafor now runs the Desert Palms sportsbook counter. He has six expressions, and his look changes when you place a ticket or try to stake more than your bankroll.
Behind the scenes, baseball, football and hockey leagues now play full seasons and playoffs alongside basketball. The sportsbook still shows demo data for now.
The 32 sportsbook teams now play out of cities across the country, from the Boston Lamplighters to the Seattle Satellites. Nicknames and team colours are unchanged.
Season lengths are set: baseball 42 games, basketball 28, football 14 and hockey 28, with every team meeting every opponent equally at home and away.

notes.title: Sportsbook lounges get their real look

items.text: The sportsbook now has its approved lounge art for all three casinos: the Palms Sports Bar, the Firelight Lounge and the Skybox. The four TV screens choose the sport, and the board under them is the menu.
Sports are named by sport (Baseball, Basketball, Football, Hockey) instead of league initials.
Your demo bet slip and tickets now stay put when you switch tables or advance the week. They're still demo only and clear if you reload the game.
A first look at the Palms Sports Bar: a new Sportsbook (demo) tab at Desert Palms with four fictional leagues, betting lines, a bet slip with singles and parlays, scores, standings, news and history.
This is a demo: teams, odds and results are placeholders, and demo bets never touch your bankroll. The real leagues and betting come later.

Each casino has its own cocktail server: Maya Solis at Desert Palms, Nina Calder at The White Buffalo and Celeste Vale at Morongo Sky. She comes by between rounds, or you can call her over. She has six expressions, and her dialogue is a draft.
Order a Tito's Double (Ryan's only drink) or water, chat, or tip her. She remembers you, and your relationship is saved like the dealers'.

Drinks add up. After a few, each one brings a random social or stamina effect, more often a bad one the more Ryan has had. When he's had too much she cuts him off, and tips can't change that; water and time do. Getting cut off repeatedly in one season gets a note from your sponsor.
Drinks never touch the games: cards, dice, the wheel and payouts are exactly as before.

notes.title: Tables side by side with the dealer

items.text: On wider screens every casino table now sits on the left, with the dealer's dialogue and the tip panel stacked on the right. The table, dealer and betting controls fit on one screen. Phones keep the stacked layout.
Bigger chips on all the tables.

notes.title: Monique stays at the roulette table

items.text: Madame Monique no longer disappears from roulette once her line is dismissed. Her portrait panel stays beside the tip panel, showing her last line, and shows the wheel spinning during spins.
Bigger dealer dialogue text at every table.
Roulette has a new table for each casino, with the wheel on the left and a clear betting board on the right, drawn from the real single-zero rules.
Every winning bet lights up after a spin, and a strip of recent winning numbers sits under the table. On phones, the betting board moves below the table so it's easy to tap.

notes.title: Men's fields early, women's fields on the LPGA path

items.text: The Amateur Circuit and SoCal Pro Series are now men's fields. From LPGA Q-School on (Q-School, Epson Tour, LPGA Tour), Ryan plays women's fields.
Kayla Brooks becomes Ryan's on-course rival once he reaches Q-School. Existing saves are updated automatically: only names change, never results, money or ratings.

notes.title: New casino tables and dealer portraits

items.text: Blackjack, Baccarat and Three Card Poker are now played at new themed tables, one look per casino: Desert Palms, The White Buffalo and Morongo Sky.
Craps gets three new full-casino tables. Only the bets this table offers are shown: Pass, Don't Pass, Odds and Field.

Dealers now appear in their dialogue box with portrait, name and relationship tier instead of standing behind the table, so the tables are the focus. The dialogue box can be collapsed to a single line.

notes.title: New casino chips and a tidier tip panel

items.text: Redrawn casino chips for all three casinos, including a proper $10 chip. Every chip is perfectly round and sharp at any screen size.
A new TIPS icon on the dealer tip panel.
The tip panel now sits beside the dealer's dialogue box instead of under it, so the table area is shorter. On phones it stacks below.

notes.title: Casino chips with each casino's own look

items.text: Desert Palms chips now carry its palm-tree design on every table, in the chip selectors and on tips. The White Buffalo and Morongo Sky have their own sets, ready for when their doors open. Values and betting are unchanged.
New screenshots and casino features on the website.
A new tip panel at every dealer table: a tip tray, $5 / $25 / $100 buttons, and your chip flies across to the dealer. The dealer answers once it lands.
Five relationship tiers with badges: Acquaintance, Regular, Friend, Confidant and Inner Circle. A banner celebrates moving up. Tips can make you a Regular; going further takes more than money.
Each dealer remembers your first tip, the tiers you've reached and how often you tip on your visits.

notes.title: Casino lobby, dealer tips and two casinos to unlock

items.text: A casino lobby with three casinos. Desert Palms is open now. The White Buffalo unlocks the first time your bank reaches $100,000, and Morongo Sky the first time it reaches $1,000,000. Unlocks are permanent, every kind of income counts, and older careers that already got there are recognised automatically. Both new casinos are opening soon.

Tip your dealers between hands: Velvet, Stick Lady, Monique, Waifu and Winston. Each remembers how much and how often you tip, reacts in their own words, and warms up to you over time. Tips never change the cards, dice or wheel, and there's no penalty for not tipping.
Each dealer shows how well they know you, from New face upward.
Greyhound races: the leader line sits in its own bar under the lanes, so the start line no longer cuts through it.

notes.title: Baccarat with Waifu and Three Card Poker with Winston

items.text: Baccarat (Punto Banco, 8 decks) with Waifu dealing. Bet Player, Banker or Tie on the felt; the standard third-card rules are applied for you. The shoe carries over between hands and visits, with a cut card and a shuffle notice, and the last 20 hands show on a bead road.

Three Card Poker with Winston: Ante and Play with an optional Pair Plus. He qualifies with queen-high, the Ante Bonus pays on straights and better when you play, and Pair Plus pays on your hand even if you fold. A dealt hand waits for you across a reload.
Both dealers talk you through the game in the same dialogue box as Monique, with their own faces and poses. Set their chat to quiet to hear only results.
The Clubhouse tab is now called Home. The Shop keeps Homes, and the Grand Clubhouse is still the top home.

notes.title: New scenery, a new roulette table, greyhound race cards, Madame Monique, new dealers and the Grand Clubhouse

items.text: New 32-bit scenery: city sunset, desert palms, coastal cliffs and casino night rotate behind the game every 90 seconds, with a crisp new header strip that fits any window size.

A new roulette table with the wheel on the right. Madame Monique runs it: she reaches across and sets the wheel spinning, reacts to big hits, and talks to you between spins in a dialogue box with her portrait. She never interrupts a spin.
Monique remembers you: streaks, big wins, how long you've been away and how your golf is going. She notices your Pink Jacket once.

Greyhound racing is a living race card: 36 dogs, each with its own running style. Every race draws a new field of six, with odds worked out from how they match up. The card stays put until its race is run, even if you leave or reload.
Animated greyhounds in their lane jackets, plus a recent-races board with your last 10 races, the odds you got and what you won or lost.
New animated dealers: Velvet Vega deals blackjack and reacts to every hand, and Stick Lady calls the craps roll and reacts to the result.
A new craps table without painted dice, so the only dice on the felt are the ones you roll, and the ON puck sits on the point.
The Grand Clubhouse: a fifth home, above the Champion's Estate, with floor-to-ceiling windows over the course. You buy it with career earnings; no major or Pink Jacket needed.
The schedule's tour badges no longer crowd the event names.
A Leave the table button at roulette.

Dry Creek's 2nd hole, Duck Pond, has new course scenery: trees beyond the boundary, flowers, reeds by the pond, a course sign, a bench and a cart. It's decoration only and never gets in the way of your shot. More courses to follow.
Madame Monique's lines are all signed off.
Big wins at the casino now get a celebration: gold coins pour down, confetti fires, and a BIG WIN (or MEGA WIN) banner counts up what you won. It works at every table, the slots and the greyhounds.
Blackjack: bigger cards, the dealer's hand on the left and yours on the right under the BLACKJACK lettering, and no more outline box around your hand.
Phase 1 Ryan's putting stroke: his hair and shirt are whole again (no more missing chunk).
The flagstick now stands in the cup instead of on top of the green.
Birdies and better: the big reaction portrait now slides in on the left, in place of the small animated reaction, so the two no longer clash and the minimap stays clear.
The Save window (and other pop-ups) always sit on top; activity cards no longer show through them.

Every dealer now talks in the same dialogue box as Madame Monique, with a portrait: Velvet Vega at blackjack and Stick Lady (the craps dealer, previously called the stickman). Stick Lady's face changes with the roll.
Ryan's dad, Baba, replaces Mom in the People tab, the weekly "Call Baba" activity and the family story events. Your existing relationship carries over.
Recent results on the Career tab: the tour badge sits on its own line above the event name instead of being squeezed beside it.
The greyhound sprites are provisional.
Greyhound racing in the casino: six dogs, 500 yards. Pick a dog, see its odds and exactly what it pays, place a win bet, and watch the race from the boxes to the line.
Every race is decided when you bet and saved with it, so the race you watch is the race that pays. Close a race halfway and it finishes and pays when you come back.
The greyhounds are placeholder art for now.

notes.title: Career Legacy and the Pink Jacket

items.text: A new Legacy tab: your trophy room, career records, a milestone timeline and your legacy status, all built from finished, verified results.
23 career milestones, from your first win to the Career Grand Slam. Milestones you already earned in an existing career are recognized with their original dates.

The season's first major is now The Desert Rose Invitational. Win it on the LPGA once Ryan reaches phase 3 to earn the Pink Jacket, with its own ceremony and a display case in your clubhouse. Your Pink Jacket count shows in Stats.
Ryan now looks right in every phase: portraits, story scenes and the on-course swing all use the approved art for the current phase.
The visor now goes with Ryan's phase, so the separate visor option is gone. Earlier results keep the event names they were played under.
Roulette at Desert Palms: a single-zero wheel with straight-up numbers (35 to 1), dozens and columns (2 to 1) and the even-money bets.
Ryan's waggle at address, putting stroke and shot reactions (celebrate, fist pumps, hands on hips, following the ball, frustration) now use the approved art for each phase.

New clubhouse rooms for every home. Up to three trophy cabinets stand along the back wall, the side walls stay clear, and the furniture sits on the floor. Cabinets you had in a corner move to the back wall automatically.
Big moments get an arcade-style close-up: an ace, an eagle, a birdie, a holed par or a par-3 green from the tee each bring up Ryan's reaction portrait.
Blackjack is played on a real table: Velvet deals from the shoe, cards slide in, chips drop on your spot, and she reacts to every hand.
Fairway Fortune is a proper cabinet: the reels spin behind the glass, pull the lever or hit the yellow button to spin, red and blue change the bet, and the lights go off on a win.
Craps is played on the felt: the point puck moves, the dice tumble across the table and the stickman calls every roll.
The casino front, logo and chips now use the Desert Palms art. Rules, odds and payouts are unchanged.

notes.title: Ryan's look and the first encounter

items.text: Ryan's look: natural curls, bald, or the auburn ponytail wig, with the visor as a separate choice. The bald look unlocks in Act II and the wig in Act III. Click Ryan's portrait to change it.
Story encounters: animated scenes with full-body characters, expression portraits, choices and real consequences. Skip jumps to the next decision and never makes one for you.
The Gold-Plated Driver: Biff Fairway III wants a long-drive bet at the range. Play the drive with a timing meter, or sim it. It's followed by The Gold-Plated Putter.
The cast: portraits and poses for Kayla, Coach Martinez, Biff, Marty, Commissioner Clipboard, Agent Reese, Mr. Dawson, Jordan, Avery and Reporter Kim.
Only one blocking screen at a time: an encounter no longer opens on top of a story, its result, a dialog or the tournament screen.
Records tab: the Albatross Leaderboard. Five views: Career, Season, All-time log, Courses (filter by course and hole) and My albatrosses.
An albatross is three under par on one hole: a par 5 in 2 or a par 4 in 1. Each one comes from a verified, finished hole score with penalty strokes included. An eagle is never counted.
Every golfer in the field can make one, not just Ryan. They're rare: about one in 15,000 to 20,000 par 5s on tour.
The ALBATROSS! celebration, with its own fanfare. Press any key or tap to skip.
Clubhouse trophies: the Albatross Ball for your first and the Five Albatross Plaque for your fifth. Plus two achievements: Albatross! and Rare Bird.
Inbox news whenever anyone in your event makes one, including Ryan's first career albatross.
Stats now count albatrosses on their own instead of as eagles.
Saves upgrade automatically. Albatrosses already in your stored results are found and added once. Nothing is added for rounds without verifiable hole scores.
Five new courses: Pacific Bluffs Links, Desert Palms Resort, Lakeside Pines CC, Skyline National and Highland Ridge. Every one has nine holes of its own.
Every event now has its own venue. Coastal events go to the links, desert events to the resort, and the majors and finales to Highland Ridge.
Each course looks the part, with its own backdrop, sky and grass: golden fescue on the coast, sandy scrub in the desert, deep pines by the lakes.
Each course plays the part too. The links are windy, the resort is scoreable and Highland Ridge is a championship test, and the whole field feels it.
The event card, the schedule and the entry screen show the course, with its par, yardage and character.
Stats: a new By course table shows your record at every venue, and the tournament log names the course.
A tree that had grown in the Dry Creek duck pond has been moved.
Stats tab: events, wins, majors, top 10s, cuts made, best finish, earnings and scoring average at a glance.
All-time money list: every golfer in the world ranked by career prize money. Start at the bottom and climb past the legends, season by season.
Scoring breakdown: low round, par 3/4/5 averages, and how every hole played out (eagles to double bogeys).
Prize money by season, a season-by-season table with your final ranking, and your record against Kayla Brooks.
Tournament log: every event Ryan has played, with a hole-by-hole scorecard for each.
Title screen menu: Continue, New Career and Load Career. Use the arrow keys, a controller, or click and tap.
New Career asks first and offers to export a backup before erasing anything.
Load Career brings back a career from a save file.
Cleaner "This week's golf" card: event name, purse, rounds and cost laid out with room to breathe, and a tidier Coming up list.
Flyover: press the ? Flyover button, F or ? (Y on a controller) to glide down the whole hole to the green, then swoop back to your ball.
Live yardage to the pin and a camera marker on the minimap during the flyover.
Casino tab: blackjack (3:2, double, split), Fairway Fortune slots and craps (Pass, Don't Pass, Odds, Field).
A night at the casino uses one of the week's activities. Lose too much and Mom will call.
Achievements: Jackpot! and High Roller.
Arcade title screen with the new Ryan's Road to the LPGA logo.
Music and sound effects: swings, impacts by club, landings, the cup, crowd reactions, cash and trophies. M mutes.
Roomier hole-result and final-result cards.
Full career RPG: train, work, rest and see friends each week; story events with choices; relationships, fame and form.
The road: Amateur Circuit → turn pro → Q-School → Epson Tour → LPGA Tour with four majors.
Stroke-play tournaments with cuts and playoffs. Pick Quick Sim, Key Holes or Full Round for each event.
Ryan's skills change how shots feel: accuracy, short game, putting, power and nerve.
Clubhouse levels: four homes, decor, bigger trophy cabinets and achievements.
32-bit course art: trees, backdrops, bunkers and water.
New 32-bit menus and on-course HUD.
Fairways no longer show a zigzag pattern; mowing stripes follow the hole.
Hand-drawn golfer sprite with a full swing, putt and reactions.
Backspin on chips and wedges: hold down while setting height.
The golfer no longer flies along with the ball.
Arcade golf in the style of 90s classics: two-click swing, draw and fade, wind, slopes and spin.
First clubhouse with a trophy cabinet, room editor and saves.
